institution: Preschool / early learning centre (provider not specified)
delivery_mode: Teacher-led classroom and supervised, play-based activity stations

tooling.primary_stack: Paper maps, picture cards, blocks, crayons, reusable craft materials, and educator-controlled display/printed media

learner_profile.description: Five-year-old preschool learners; activities are oral, visual, movement-based, and supported by an educator or caregiver.
prior_knowledge: Can listen to a short read-aloud
Can notice and compare simple shapes, pictures, and quantities
learner_profile.reading_level: Preschool read-aloud; adult scribing and picture cues required

example_contexts: Chinese New Year, Hari Raya, Deepavali, and Christmas

competencies.title: Find Singapore and discover its port
scope: Singapore as a small island city-state
Singapore's location on regional sea routes
A port as a place where ships load, unload, and transfer goods

performance_criteria.text: Point to Singapore on a simple picture map with educator support.
Use a toy ship or picture to show that ships travel between places by sea.
Describe a port as a place where people move goods on or off ships, using a simple example.

competencies.title: Notice Singapore's gardens and green spaces
scope: A city can include plants and green spaces
Gardens by the Bay Supertrees are human-made structures with plants
Ways people can care for plants and shared green spaces

performance_criteria.text: Identify a plant or green space in a photograph or model.
Explain that a Supertree is a human-made structure with plants, not a living tree.
Choose and demonstrate one age-appropriate way to care for a shared green space.

competencies.title: Meet the Merlion and its story
scope: The Merlion's lion head and fish body
The Merlion as a Singapore symbol and statue
The story linking the fish to Singapore's early fishing settlement and the lion to its name and legend

performance_criteria.text: Describe or assemble the Merlion's lion head and fish body.
Recognise the Merlion as a symbol represented by a statue, not a real animal.
Retell one part of the Merlion story and identify it as a story about Singapore's past.

competencies.title: Celebrate Singapore's many communities
scope: People in Singapore have varied cultures, languages, and family traditions
Chinese New Year, Hari Raya, Deepavali, and Christmas as examples of celebrations observed by some communities
Sharing food and treating different traditions respectfully

performance_criteria.text: Name or match at least two celebrations to picture cues without claiming everyone celebrates them.
Share one respectful question or observation about a tradition, language, or food.
Take turns in a shared food or celebration sorting activity.

competencies.title: Explore Singapore's airport and inventions
scope: Jewel Changi Airport's Rain Vortex as an indoor waterfall
How people use design and technology to make places useful and interesting
Shared responsibility for caring for clean public places

performance_criteria.text: Identify the Rain Vortex as an indoor waterfall at Jewel Changi Airport.
Use blocks or a drawing to show one way people design a useful public place.
Choose one action that helps keep a shared public place clean and explain why it helps.

assessments.name: Singapore Explorer Show-and-Tell
assessments.deliverable: A group-made Singapore explorer board or model, plus an individual short oral or picture-supported reflection
assessments.notes: Educator-mediated AI only; children contribute predictions and critique printed, age-appropriate outputs. Do not expose children to public chat interfaces or enter personal data.

assumptions: The source is an informal child-facing explainer, not a formal module specification; a six-week, 17-contact-hour preschool module is assumed to make it teachable.
The five competencies are derived from the explainer's five teachable themes: port/location, green spaces, Merlion, cultural communities, and airport/design.
Each competency is allocated 1 theory hour and 2 practical hours; 2 practical hours are reserved for the final project assessment. No separate revision block is added.
Institution, module code, framework, duration, workload, delivery mode, marker ratio, and learner prerequisites were not stated; values in this brief are planning defaults, not source facts.
The six-week duration is rounded to two calendar months for the schema.
The 40% AI-assist target and 2-hour lab block follow the orchestrator defaults; 7 hours is ceil(17 × 40%).

The AI target is unusually high for five-year-olds. All AI use is educator-mediated, off-screen where feasible, and limited to vetted, printed outputs; children do not use public AI chat tools directly. Provider safeguarding approval is required before delivery.
Performance criteria are derived from the source themes and marked derived; no standards framework or supplied criteria were provided.
A single 2-hour group project assessment carries 100% because no assessment scheme was supplied; individual evidence is collected through each child's contribution and reflection.
Project AI policy defaults to allowed-with-citation, adapted with educator mediation for the age group.

The source's descriptions are simplified. Teaching materials should distinguish Singapore as an island city-state, describe the Supertrees as structures rather than trees, avoid claims that everyone celebrates or speaks the same way, and identify the Merlion as a symbol/statue rather than a magical creature.
No named school, class size, accessibility needs, approved AI platform, or media permissions were supplied; the educator must check these before delivery.
